newsitem.title: UK: Britain would veto EU fuel tax plan - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: Britain would veto EU fuel tax plan - Clarke.

text.p: Finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday Britain would veto proposals by the European Commission which would raise minimum tax levels for some fuel sources and introduce them for others.
The Commission on Wednesday agreed a draft directive which would mean that EU member states would for the first time be forced to tax electricity and natural gas.
"The United Kingdom can veto tax proposals which are unacceptable to us, and we would not hesitate to use our veto if these proposals stay in their present form," Clarke said in a statement.
"I think that it is important to make this clear straightaway, before we even start detailed discussions in the Council of Finance Ministers."
"The UK would veto proposals...if they required the UK to introduce new taxes on gas, electricity and coal."
The draft directive foresees introduction of a minimum tax on electricity of one 1 Ecu ($1.14) per megawatt hour in 1998, rising to three Ecus in 2002.
Natural gas would be taxed at 2.9 Ecus per gigajoule in 1998 when it is used as a motor fuel and at 0.2 Ecus when it is used for heating.
The plan is fiercely opposed by industry, particularly the chemical and automobile sectors which use energy heavily. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
